summary: The study reports the growth of silica (SiO2) and alumina (Al2O3) nanolayers on GaAs, InAs, and InSb substrates using atomic layer deposition (ALD). The process involves self-limiting chemisorption of metal halides and water vapor under limiting surface coverage conditions. The growth temperature and surface reactivity of hydroxyl groups are critical factors influencing the layer-by-layer growth of the nanolayers. The dielectric properties of the nanolayers were evaluated, and the results indicate that the ALD process can be used to fabricate high-quality dielectric structures for micro- and nanoelectronic applications.
